facts.fact: The Press Union of Liberia, the Center for Media Studies and several civil society groups, with the opposition CDC and the Liberia National Bar Association also named, criticised the cyberbullying, false information and offensive communication provisions of the Cybercrime Act as vague and as a weapon to silence critics.

Police arrested Jerry Nyanti Wratto in Monrovia, charged him and sent him to court under sections 10.1, 15.1, 18.1 and 19.1 of the Cybercrime Act for Facebook and TikTok posts calling the Vice President names, accusing him of corruption and questioning his credentials; the article gives the arrest only as 'this week' of its 2026-09-24 date.
